{{2017–18 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2017–18 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] for the 42nd consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 20,500. The team, led by [[John Calipari]] in his ninth season as head coach, was a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]].

On January 22, 2018, following losses to [[2017–18 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] on the road, and to [[2017–18 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] at home, the Wildcats fell out of the [[AP Poll|AP rankings]] for the first time since March 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-rankings-kentucky-falls-out-of-ap-top-25-poll-for-1st-time-since-2014/|title=College basketball rankings: Kentucky falls out of AP Top 25 poll for 1st time since 2014|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2018-01-22|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article195942174.html|title=Top 25 doesn't include the Cats. Remember what happened last time UK dropped out?|work=kentucky|access-date=2018-01-22|language=en}}</ref>

They finished the season 26–11, 10–8 in SEC play to finish in three-way tie for fourth place. They defeated [[2017–18 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], [[2017–18 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], and [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] to become champions of the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]]. They earned the SEC's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they defeated [[2017–18 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]] and [[2017–18 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen where they lost to [[2017–18 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]].

== Previous season ==
The [[2016–17 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 32–6, 16–2 in [[2016–17 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to win the regular season SEC championship. In the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] the Wildcats beat [[2016–17 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], [[2016–17 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], and [[2016–17 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, the Wildcats received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a No. 2 seed in the South region, they defeated No. 15 [[2016–17 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/march-madness/index.ssf/2017/03/kentucky_vs_northern_kentucky.html|title=Freshmen lead Kentucky over Northern Kentucky: NCAA Tournament first round|work=OregonLive.com|access-date=2017-08-07|language=en-US}}</ref> and No. 10 [[2016–17 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] to advance to the Sweet 16.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400947227|title=Wichita State vs. Kentucky - Game Recap - March 19, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-08-07}}</ref> There, they defeated No. 3 [[2016–17 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] to advance to the Elite Eight<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400947330|title=UCLA vs. Kentucky - Game Recap - March 24, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-08-07}}</ref> where they lost to eventual National Champion, No. 1 [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/march-madness/index.ssf/2017/03/kentucky_vs_north_carolina_liv.html|title=North Carolina holds off Kentucky, moves on to Final Four: NCAA Tournament live updates recap, highlights, score, stats|work=OregonLive.com|access-date=2017-08-07|language=en-US}}</ref>

===2017–18 newcomers===
[[Nick Richards]], a native of [[Kingston, Jamaica|Kingston]], [[Jamaica]] who moved to [[Queens|Queens, New York]] in 2013, was the first commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on November 10 at a press conference at his high school.<ref name=NRPWcommit-2>{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114023728.html|title=Kentucky lands commitments from a pair of five-star basketball recruits|access-date=2016-11-10|date=2016-11-10|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 14 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

[[P. J. Washington]], a [[Dallas]] native attending school in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas, Nevada]], was the second commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on November 10 live on [[ESPNU]].<ref name="NRPWcommit-2" /> He chose Kentucky over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 15 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

[[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]], originally from [[Hamilton, Ontario]] and attending school in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]], was the third commitment in the Kentucky class.  He committed to Kentucky on November 14 through a message on [[Twitter]].<ref name=NRPWcommit>{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114610083.html|title=Calipari adds third commitment to Kentucky's recruiting class of 2017|access-date=2016-11-14|date=2016-11-14|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref>  He was a consensus top fifty player, ranked No. 42 by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 24/7 Sports.

[[Quade Green]], from [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], was the fourth commitment in the Kentucky class. He signed his National Letter of Intent on November 16, the last day of the early signing period, but did not reveal his choice between Kentucky and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] until an event at his high school on November 19 - with his mother Tamika Johnson by his side.<ref name=greencommit>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Ben |title=New UK commitment Quade Green will bring 'Philly toughness' to Lexington |newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=November 19, 2016 |url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article115990473.html |access-date=November 21, 2016}}</ref> He was a consensus top-25 player and ranked as a five-star player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 24/7 Sports.

[[Hamidou Diallo]], a Queens native who graduated from a Connecticut school in spring 2016, announced on January 7, 2017, that he would enroll at UK for the start of the school's spring semester the following week. While he was eligible to play immediately, he redshirted the spring semester and began play as a freshman in 2017–18.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18427587/five-star-wing-hamidou-diallo-commits-kentucky-wildcats-enroll-next-week |title=Hamidou Diallo, No. 11 in ESPN 100, picks Kentucky over UConn |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |work=ESPN.com |date=January 7, 2017 |access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

Jemarl Baker, a native of [[Eastvale, California]], was the seventh commitment in the Kentucky recruiting class. He announced his decision on April 11 via a story posted on Scout.com by Evan Daniels.<ref name=bakecommit>{{Cite news |last=Daniels |first=Evan |title=Four-star guard Jemarl Baker commits to Kentucky |website=Scout |date=April 11, 2017|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1769972-jemarl-baker-commits-kentucky |access-date=April 11, 2017}}</ref> Baker originally committed to [[Cuonzo Martin]] at [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], before Martin left the school to coach [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]]. He averaged 17.1 points, 4.1 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.8 steals for Roosevelt High School in Corona, Calif., and he quickly emerged as one of the Wildcats' top backcourt targets after their season ended last month. Scout.com ranks Baker as the No. 86 overall prospect in the 2017 class.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Roberts|first1=Ben|title=New basketball commitment Jemarl Baker is 'exactly what Kentucky needed'|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article143944139.html|newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader|access-date=April 24, 2017}}</ref>

UK's final commitment came on May 6, when [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]] product [[Kevin Knox II]] announced he would come to the school. Kentucky beat out Duke, Florida State, North Carolina, and Missouri for Knox's signature.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/19326360/kevin-knox-five-star-recruit-chooses-kentucky-florida-state-duke-north-carolina |title=Kevin Knox, No. 9-ranked prospect in 2017, commits to Kentucky |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |work=ESPN.com |date=May 6, 2017 |access-date=May 6, 2017}}</ref>

===2018–19 newcomers===
[[Immanuel Quickley]], from [[Havre de Grace, Maryland]], was the first commitment in the Kentucky's 2018 class. He committed to Kentucky on September 22, over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]]. He was a consensus five-star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 12 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

The Wildcats' second 2018 commitment was [[Keldon Johnson]], a small forward from [[South Hill, Virginia]], who committed on November 11. Kentucky beat out [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] for Johnson's signature. He was also a consensus five-star prospect, and ranked by ESPN as its No. 7 overall prospect.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/21380165/keldon-johnson-no-7-recruit-espn-100-commits-kentucky-wildcats |title=Keldon Johnson, No. 7 recruit in ESPN 100, joins Kentucky's 2018 class |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 11, 2017 |access-date=November 12, 2017}}</ref>

Tyler Herro was the third commitment for Kentucky's 2018 class. Formerly committed to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], Herro committed to Kentucky the week after his official visit. Herro was a consensus four-star prospect and was ranked the No. 4 shooting guard in the 2018 class by ESPN.

E.J. Montgomery was the fourth commitment for Kentucky's 2018 class. Former committed to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], he re-opened his recruitment after the Auburn staff was implicated in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]]. Montgomery committed to Kentucky on April 9, 2018. Montgomery was a five-star prospect and was ranked No. 12 in the 2018 class.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23088894/ej-montgomery-latest-5-star-recruit-commit-kentucky-wildcats |title=E.J. Montgomery latest 5-star recruit to commit to Kentucky|first=Jeff |last=Borzello |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=April 9, 2018 |access-date=April 9, 2018}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
On June 6, 2017, Kentucky released the non-conference portion of its schedule.<ref name="schedule">{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/uk-men-s-basketball-unveils-2017-18-nonconference-schedule-06-06-2017|title=UK Men's Basketball Unveils 2017-18 Nonconference Schedule|date=2016-06-06|work=UKathletics.com|publisher=JMI Sports|access-date=2016-06-07|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610035217/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/uk-men-s-basketball-unveils-2017-18-nonconference-schedule-06-06-2017|archive-date=2017-06-10}}</ref> The schedule is highlighted by marquee match-ups at Rupp Arena and across the country. Kentucky traveled to Chicago to play Kansas in the annual Champions Classic, to New York to play Monmouth, to New Orleans to play against UCLA in the annual CBS Sports Classic, and finally to face in-state rival Louisville in Lexington. Kentucky also hosted Virginia Tech and traveled to play West Virginia in the Big 12/SEC Challenge.

Big Blue Madness took place on October 13. The event was the debut of the team for the 2017–18 season. The annual Blue-White game took place on October 20, 2017.
